body.prose:
An element of a holon's interior has the shape of a holon at a smaller scale: an id of its own, unique within the holon it stands in, written `$id`; what it is an instance of, as references to types, written `{ "$ref": … }` as any reference in a body is, where a version holds bare ids; and a body, checked against those types at commit as any holon's is. Its type may be fixed by what holds it, as a brief's prose is [Paragraphs](ref:01M6MFK1NEH46R8YJVFSQ5Q3BT) unless an element says otherwise, so it is said only where it differs. Each element brings its own small type, which is what keeps a deep structure typed: no type knows more than its own level.

An interior element is in no index as a holon of its own and travels with its holon. The day it needs a life of its own it is lifted, given an identity in the field and versions, and keeps what it already is.

*The author's, 2026-11-05: if it is interior, do we work with reserved JSON names, for we would have no type structure anymore; can we even type such structures. The shape at a smaller scale the session's answer, shown him in a piece of the store brief.*
body.title: Holons at a smaller scale
